edges.description: Milia form during healing of subepidermal blisters.
Blisters in the mechanobullous form heal with atrophic scars.

Repeated blistering of trauma-prone sites damages the nails.
Healed blisters leave post-inflammatory hyper- and hypopigmentation.
Mucosal esophageal blistering heals with stricture.
Conjunctival blistering heals with scarring that can impair vision.

nodes.description: Autoreactive B cells and plasma cells produce IgG autoantibodies against type VII collagen, mostly recognizing epitopes within its non-collagenous NC1 domain. These autoantibodies are directly pathogenic.

nodes.description: Passive transfer of anti-type VII collagen IgG into mice reproduces subepidermal blistering; gene-knockout strains dissect the complement and neutrophil effector steps.

nodes.description: Anti-COL7 IgG binds type VII collagen in the anchoring fibrils at the dermal-epidermal junction, producing linear IgG deposits. Binding has two consequences that define the two clinical variants: it directly impairs anchoring-fibril function (mechanobullous) and it triggers complement and neutrophil recruitment (inflammatory).
